bullets.title: Samsung Foundry hikes 4nm prices 10-15%; full capacity signal
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flagged that Samsung Foundry raised SF4 (4nm) node prices 10-15% month-over-month in July-August for US and China clients, with Pyeongtaek operating at full capacity since late last year. Chinese customers are reportedly accepting the largest increases. This is a meaningful signal on foundry pricing power and downstream cost pass-through risk for chipmakers.

bullets.title: Asia tech plunges: KOSPI -6%, ChiNext -6%, STAR 50 -7%, Nikkei -3.2%
bullets.body: Asia tech indices suffered a 'proper tech puke' overnight per multiple accounts, with KOSPI down 5.8-6%, ChiNext -6%, STAR 50 -7%, and Japan's Nikkei off 3.2%, breaking Hedgeye TRADE Signal Support for the second time in two months. One account noted the KOSPI is now 29% off its recent peak, flagging '#MOAB Semis peak' language.

bullets.title: Global bond yields at highest since 2008; macro headwinds mount
bullets.body: Global bond yields rose to their highest level since 2008, per fintwit commentary, compounding the macro pressure on equities. NY Fed Services PMI saw double-digit declines in business activity and climate components in August, with six-month expectations turning more pessimistic.

bullets.title: SPY correction from ATH on decelerating volume; buy-dips regime intact
bullets.body: Hedgeye noted SPY's 3-day correction from all-time highs is occurring on decelerating volume, distinguishing current August action from July's Quad4 environment. The current regime is characterized as an 'Investable Bucket Vol Regime' with a sell-rips/buy-dips tactical stance, not a systemic breakdown.

bullets.title: High beta momentum stocks -6.4% yesterday; healthcare +1.6% outperforms
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged high beta momentum names down another 6.4% on Tuesday while their long healthcare (XLV) position gained 1.6%, highlighting sharp sector rotation away from momentum/risk. Retail investor portfolios reportedly flat YTD and down 4% on the day.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings: 458 companies report +50% aggregate YoY growth
bullets.body: Hedgeye noted that 458 S&P 500 companies have reported earnings with an aggregate year-over-year growth of 50%, which they cite as driving the broadening rally to all-time highs before the current pullback.

bullets.title: Macro FX: veteran trader long EUR + JPY simultaneously—rare 27-year first
bullets.body: A fintwit veteran noted being long both Euros and Yen simultaneously—described as an exceedingly rare positioning in a 27-year career—while separately reiterating a short USD view. Gold long vs. short USD cited as the current alpha trade over bitcoin.

bullets.title: Import/export prices decelerating; housing demand weakening
bullets.body: July import prices rose 5.9% YoY (down from 6.7%) and export prices +8.2% YoY (down from 10.0%), suggesting sequential inflation deceleration. Pending home sales fell 2.5% YoY in July—entering negative territory for the first time since January—with all four regions declining, led by the West (-4.7% m/m).

bullets.title: U.S.-made semiconductors and optical modules commanding pricing premium
bullets.body: Fintwit commentary noted that U.S.-manufactured products now command a premium in the current tariff environment, specifically calling out AAOI's U.S.-made optical modules and Micron's domestic DRAM as beneficiaries, with hyperscalers reportedly willing to pay up for U.S.-sourced supply.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR growth slows; Anthropic doubles revenue and pulls ahead
bullets.body: OpenAI's Q2 revenue grew 18% YoY to $6.7B, while Anthropic's revenue more than doubled to $11.6B—surpassing OpenAI for the first time. Separately, July showed acceleration in combined ARR for both companies, with a note that Anthropic may have shifted to net ARR reporting ahead of a potential IPO, making the $65B net figure more conservative than prior gross metrics.

bullets.title: Amazon drone delivery expanding to ~500 U.S. cities; Chicago and Atlanta added
bullets.body: Amazon Prime Air has already delivered 'hundreds of thousands of packages' in 2024 and is expanding to suburban Chicago and Atlanta as the program transitions from R&D to commercial operations, with plans to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns.

bullets.title: Cerebras CS-4 claims 30x faster AI inference than GPU systems
bullets.body: Cerebras announced its CS-4 AI accelerator, claiming up to 30x faster inference than GPU systems. This is a direct competitive claim against GPU incumbents and worth monitoring for implications on AI infrastructure spending priorities.

bullets.title: Intel Nova Lake-S ES leaks; alleged chip faster than all current-gen Intel CPUs
bullets.body: A leaked Intel Core Ultra 9 4950K engineering sample points to a new naming scheme for Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs and is reportedly faster than all current-generation Intel CPUs in early benchmarks.

bullets.title: Chip stocks steady ahead of Fed minutes; markets in wait-and-see mode
bullets.body: Fintwit noted chip stocks holding steady as markets await release of Fed meeting minutes, with bonds also flat. The session framed as a pause in the broader risk-off move from Asia overnight.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk elevated: China Taiwan drills, Iran Europe threat, Saudi dark-sail
bullets.body: Three concurrent geopolitical signals flagged: China deployed 20 warplanes and 7 warships near Taiwan; Iran reportedly weighing strikes on U.S. targets in Europe (Bulgaria, Cyprus); Saudi Arabia selling oil near Oman, suggesting dark-sailing tankers through Hormuz. Brent and WTI futures up over 1% to highest since late July.
